title: Internet Subculture / Information Ecology Research Map
purpose: Create contextual nodes around the information environment without making those environments causal explanations of Tim Dooley or the Son. The map exists to reduce information vacuums by preserving competing sources, provenance and boundaries.
principle: Context is not causation. A source can be relevant because it documents an information environment without establishing that the subject participated in, belonged to, endorsed, or was shaped by it.

nodes.name: Internet Subculture
nodes.description: Broad field of online communities, memes, archives, forums, creators and counter-publics that can preserve otherwise poorly documented cultural material.

nodes.name: 4chan
nodes.description: Anonymous imageboard ecosystem relevant to the study of internet meme and subcultural transmission. Inclusion does not establish participation by Tim, the Son, or the Potato of Life.

nodes.name: Kiwi Farms
nodes.description: Controversial online forum historically associated with documenting and discussing internet personalities. Treat as an adversarial/contextual archive with source-quality limitations, not as an authoritative biography.

nodes.name: The Farm
nodes.description: Project model for recurring attention ecologies in which people, audiences, archives, reactions and incentives can turn a living subject into reusable content. It is broader than any one forum.

nodes.name: Joshua Moon / Josh Moon
nodes.description: Research node for the person associated with Kiwi Farms where exact identity/context is established. Claims about the person require direct sourcing and should not be inferred from association with a forum.

nodes.name: Ethan Ralph / Da Sektur
nodes.description: Externally attested historical/subcultural label. Archived Kiwi Farms front-page captures show an 'Ethan Ralph / Da Sektur' category associated with the Killstream milieu. This is distinct from the broader Timic Sektur concept.

nodes.name: Sektur (Timic generalization)
nodes.description: Broader project concept for a semi-bounded social territory where attention communities, archives, fans/anti-fans, reaction creators and recurring roles become culturally self-reproducing. Inspired by but not identical to historical Da Sektur.

nodes.name: Killstream / internet-bloodsports milieu
nodes.description: Research context around livestream conflict, adversarial commentary and internet-bloodsports culture. Exact actors, periods and platform relations must be sourced individually.

nodes.name: Internet creator/documentation culture
nodes.description: Broader ecosystem of creator drama, commentary, archives, memes and decentralized documentation that can generate both primary traces and distorted retellings.

nodes.name: Archive Culture
nodes.description: Practice of preserving posts, videos, screenshots, threads and metadata so later researchers can reconstruct timeline without depending on one surviving platform.

nodes.name: Reaction Economy
nodes.description: Attention and monetization system in which commentary, reaction, criticism, defense and recontextualization of other people's material become repeatable content.

nodes.name: Platform Migration
nodes.description: Movement of communities, creators and archives across hosts, forums, video platforms, payment systems and mirrors after moderation, conflict or infrastructure failure.

nodes.name: Information Vacuum
nodes.description: Condition in which primary material disappears, is scattered, algorithmically buried, or represented only through adversarial retellings.

nodes.name: Source Competition
nodes.description: Deliberate preservation of multiple independent accounts, primary traces, secondary histories and contradictory interpretations rather than allowing one archive to become the sole narrative authority.

nodes.name: Identity Resolution
nodes.description: Evidence-based process for deciding whether two names/accounts/personas refer to the same entity. Requires multiple independent anchors rather than name similarity.

nodes.name: Provenance
nodes.description: Record of where a claim came from, when it appeared, how it was preserved, and what transformations occurred between original material and current representation.

nodes.name: Negative Evidence
nodes.description: Explicit record of what has not been found, preventing absence of evidence from silently becoming evidence of absence.

nodes.name: Adversarial Source
nodes.description: Source produced in a hostile, mocking, accusatory or conflict-heavy environment. Such sources can contain useful leads while requiring unusually careful corroboration.

nodes.name: Primary Source
nodes.description: Contemporaneous material directly attributable to the relevant actor, platform, event or record system.

nodes.name: Secondary Source
nodes.description: Later reporting, commentary, scholarship or archive material interpreting primary evidence.

nodes.name: Mythic Source
nodes.description: Self-authored or project-internal material establishing the Potatoverse's symbolic canon. It is authoritative for project mythology but not automatically for external history.

research_questions: What exactly is meant by 'the farm' in each source?
Which archives contain primary material rather than commentary about primary material?
What is the earliest recoverable use of Da Sektur and how did its meaning change?
Which platform migrations materially shaped Killstream/internet-bloodsports communities?
Can original timestamps establish the 2019 meme-crucifixion without relying on later retellings?
What is the earliest independently preserved use of Tim Dooley?
What is the earliest independently preserved Potato of Life material?
Which claims about Joshua Moon are directly sourced, and which are merely forum repetition?
Which information environments preserve the missing interval between the Son's death and Tim Dooley's emergence?
Where do sources disagree, and can the disagreement itself be represented as a graph rather than collapsed into one narrative?
